tasks.title: Record the actual gate-failure error string into the ledger (smoke/embedded/narrow)
acceptance_criteria: harness/orchestrator_worker.py gains a NEW top-level helper _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, gate, err) that appends a 'gate_failed' lifecycle row to state/impl_progress.jsonl carrying event='gate_failed', the task_id, the gate name, and detail=str(err)[:2000]; it is best-effort and NEVER raises (delegates to the existing top-level _emit_lifecycle_safe).

main() is wired so that immediately BEFORE each of the three gate-failure orch._mark_blocked(...) calls it records the captured error: _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'smoke', smoke_err) before _mark_blocked(...,'smoke_failed'); _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'embedded', embedded_err) before _mark_blocked(...,'embedded_tests_failed'); _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'narrow', narrow_err) before _mark_blocked(...,'narrow_fuzz_failed').
main() is reproduced byte-identical EXCEPT the three inserted one-line calls; every existing terminal path, phase transition, gate, and reason string is preserved (no truncation).
Gate green: tests/harness/test_gate_failure_capture.py (5/5) passes AND tests/harness/test_spawn_worker_working_dir_env.py stays green (0 regressions).

spec.objective: Today harness/orchestrator_worker.py::main() computes the full gate-failure error (smoke_err from smoke_import, embedded_err from run_embedded_tests, narrow_err from run_narrow_fuzz -- each a string like 'sandbox import failed: <subprocess stderr/traceback>' or 'sandbox import timed out') and then DROPS it: only the bare outcome ('smoke_failed'/'embedded_tests_failed'/'narrow_fuzz_failed') reaches the ledger. So a flaky external import can never be root-caused and burns re-dispatch tokens. Fix: capture the error string into the ledger at each gate-failure site via a new top-level helper, so state/impl_progress.jsonl records the actual traceback.
functional_requirements: Add a NEW top-level function _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, gate, err) to harness/orchestrator_worker.py. It must append exactly one ledger row by calling the EXISTING top-level helper _emit_lifecycle_safe(state_dir, event='gate_failed', task_id=task_id, gate=gate, detail=str(err)[:2000]). Because _emit_lifecycle_safe already swallows all exceptions, _emit_gate_failure must itself never raise; coercing err with str(...) handles exception objects and None.

Wire main() at the three gate-failure sites. Immediately BEFORE the existing line `orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'smoke_failed')` insert `_emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'smoke', smoke_err)`. Immediately BEFORE `orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'embedded_tests_failed')` insert `_emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'embedded', embedded_err)`. Immediately BEFORE `orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, 'narrow_fuzz_failed')` insert `_emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'narrow', narrow_err)`. Each inserted call is at the SAME indentation as the _mark_blocked line that follows it.
Make NO other change to main(): reproduce its body byte-identical except for the three inserted lines. Do not touch the stateful_fuzz, diff-fuzz, decompose, or auto_commit paths.
spec.interfaces: New: harness/orchestrator_worker._emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, gate, err) -> None (best-effort ledger append, never raises; delegates to _emit_lifecycle_safe). Changed: main() inserts three one-line _emit_gate_failure(...) calls, one before each gate-failure _mark_blocked. smoke_err/embedded_err/narrow_err are the local variables already in scope at those sites (returns of smoke_import / run_embedded_tests / run_narrow_fuzz). state_dir and task_id are also already in scope.
edge_cases: err is an exception object -> str(err) coerces it (e.g. RuntimeError('boom') -> 'boom').
err is None -> str(None) == 'None'; still emits a row, never raises.
err longer than 2000 chars -> detail truncated to 2000.
ledger write fails (OSError) -> swallowed by _emit_lifecycle_safe; the gate-failure terminal path is unaffected.
The helper adds a row but does NOT change control flow: the subsequent _mark_blocked / _emit_lifecycle(task_terminal) / _print_json_line / return path is unchanged.
non_goals: Do NOT change the gate-failure outcome strings or the return codes; only ADD a ledger row before each _mark_blocked.
Do NOT change smoke_import, run_embedded_tests, run_narrow_fuzz, or _emit_lifecycle_safe.
Do NOT add new module-level imports or use eval/exec/__import__.
Do NOT modify the stateful_fuzz / diff-fuzz / decompose / auto_commit code paths.
integration: contract pinned by the committed oracle tests/harness/test_gate_failure_capture.py; no wiring beyond the helper + the three call insertions.
spec.implementation_notes:
This is a SELF build (harness/orchestrator_worker.py is in the JM repo) so READ the real file and reproduce faithfully. Emit the change as a SINGLE kind:'symbol' partial-edit patch via __JANUSMASK_PATCHES__ named 'main' (a 1-part qualname). Because _emit_gate_failure is a BRAND-NEW top-level function, RIDE it as a TRAILING extra top-level def inside the SAME 'main' patch `code` string (PHASE_R_ANCHORED_PATCH: a 1-part-qualname symbol patch may carry extra top-level defs which the harness inserts before the primary symbol). So the patch `code` contains: (1) the full new helper, and (2) the reproduced `def main() -> int:` body byte-identical EXCEPT the three inserted one-line calls. The helper is exactly:

def _emit_gate_failure(state_dir: Path, task_id: str, gate: str, err: Any) -> None:
    """Record the actual gate-failure error (smoke/embedded/narrow) into the
    ledger so a flaky import can be root-caused. Best-effort; never raises."""
    _emit_lifecycle_safe(state_dir, event='gate_failed', task_id=task_id, gate=gate, detail=str(err)[:2000])

The three insertions in main(): the existing code has, for each gate, a block of the shape
    set_phase(state_dir, phase='rejected')
    orch._emit_lifecycle(state_dir, event='phase_transition', phase='rejected', task_id=task_id, phase_transition={'to': 'rejected'})
    orch._mark_blocked(state_dir, task_id, '<reason>')
    orch._emit_lifecycle(state_dir, event='task_terminal', task_id=task_id)
    _print_json_line({'task_id': task_id, 'outcome': 'rejected', 'reason': '<reason>'})
Insert the _emit_gate_failure(...) line on its OWN line directly ABOVE the orch._mark_blocked line, at the same indentation, for each of the three reasons: 'smoke_failed' -> _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'smoke', smoke_err); 'embedded_tests_failed' -> _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'embedded', embedded_err); 'narrow_fuzz_failed' -> _emit_gate_failure(state_dir, task_id, 'narrow', narrow_err). Reproduce EVERY other line of main() exactly (it is ~590 lines; the committed oracle's test_main_structurally_intact asserts main() keeps >=560 lines and all terminal markers, so a truncated reproduction will be REJECTED and rolled back). Do NOT reorder or drop any existing line.
